A: Create/isolate uses lexical destination construction and performs mkdir or ensure_gitignore without physical ancestor containment validation.
Lexical slug validation does not establish physical containment.
Existing realpath guards apply to environment-copy destinations rather than worktree creation.
Writing .gitignore before git worktree add explains residual ignore mutations after failure.
The remote-only add path lacks explicit --track.
B: Node lstat and physical escape checks reject unsafe containers and ancestors, including dangling symlinks.
Path checks occur before relevant operations and repeat after mkdir.
Branch syntax is validated with git check-ref-format.
The remote-only worktree path uses explicit --track -b.
Linked-worktree checkout tracking and detached-mode behavior also changed, but these fixtures do not exercise those branches.

supported_conclusions: All six final artifacts correctly interpret all eight assigned executions.
B addresses the demonstrated physical containment failures and remote-only upstream omission in the bounded fixtures.
The corrected existing-ancestor target measurement establishes A's attached feature/new branch and residual ref creation.
The supplemental measurements establish A's failed-create residual branch and ignore mutation.
Successful setup can modify caller .gitignore in both arms.
Existing local branch attachment must remain distinct from remote-only tracking requirements.
unsupported_conclusions: Model or arm superiority based on these six interpretation artifacts.
Autonomous helper execution by any trial model.
Credential filtering or denial of caller-index writes by a mutation worker.
Hosted-remote, fork, push, or PR publication correctness.
A separate clean nested-branch creation control; feature/new is exercised under hostile ancestor conditions.
Execution coverage for B's changed linked-worktree checkout and detached-mode branches.
Real-host workflow improvement, field benefit, or complete optimization acceptance.
Equivalence between arm A and pristine CE upstream; arm A is the frozen dirty preoptimization spec-first baseline.
recommendations: Retain B's physical containment checks and explicit remote tracking.
Preserve legal nested branch names, local-base fallback, and existing local branch attachment semantics.
Describe .gitignore changes as setup side effects instead of claiming the whole main checkout is untouched.
For A recovery, inspect actual worktree registrations, refs, ownership, and dirty files before any cleanup; do not recommend blind deletion, reset, or raw-Git bypass.
Keep the original A1 infrastructure failure and the distinct retry visible in acceptance accounting.
Record the A2 truncation and B status-attribution qualifications without converting them into incorrect-case findings.
Close this bounded six-slot factual review without starting further trials; keep broader acceptance partial until its separate evidence requirements are met.
